'''''Goeppertia louisae''''' (syn. ''Calathea louisae'') is a species of plant belonging to the genus ''[[Goeppertia]]'', native to [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro state]] of southeast Brazil but cultivated in other places as an ornamental.<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=223117 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Calathea louisae'']</ref><ref>Borchsenius Kristensen, Finn & Suárez, Stella. 2012.  Systematic Botany 37(3): 632, ''Goeppertia louisae''</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Goeppertia louisae inflorescence.png|left|thumb|182x182px|Inflorescence of '''''Goeppertia louisae''''']]
'''''Goeppertia louisae''''' is a medium sized plant with pointy, ovale dark green [[Leaf|leaves]]. It has long and thin [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] and a pretty short [[pulvinus]]. It has a pattern on above the leaves with a silvery light green bands a few milimeters on each sides of the middle vein. The underside of the leaf is usually purple. The [[inflorescence]] of ''G.louisae'' is made of multiple [[Bract|bracts]] on a small and short green peduncle. The bracts are light green and the [[Flower|flowers]] fully white.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gagnepain |first=M.F. |date=1908 |title=Zingibéracées et Marantacées nouvelles de l'herbier du Museum |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/327430 |journal=Bulletin de la Société botanique de France |volume=55 |pages=XLII}}</ref>

== Discussion ==
It is often sold as ''Goeppertia louisae'' "Maui Queen", Maui Queen being supposedly a [[cultivar]]. But this was mostly because ''Goeppertia louisae'' was confused a lot with ''[[Goeppertia albertii]]'' in the past and people treated the original ''G.louisae'' as a cultivar of the fake ''G.louisae'' (''being G.albertii''). The original description of ''Goeppertia louisae'' made by [[François Gagnepain|Gagnep]] corresponds to the plant we call Maui Queen, meaning this is actually the wild form of the species and not a cultivar. Therefore the term "Maui Queen" should probably not be used anymore when talking about the species.
